title: Future Warming Decreases Irrigation‐Induced Yield Benefits in Global Food Production
content:
Abstract

Irrigation has enabled higher and more stable food production than when farmers relied only on rainfed cropping systems in the past. However, its future benefits may diminish under climate change due to increasing crop water demand and constraints on water availability. Here, we compare crop yields between irrigated and rainfed conditions on currently irrigated cropland. We use an integrated crop and water model under multiple climate scenarios up to 2100 and quantify their differences as an indicator of the irrigation effect. We find that the irrigation effect on yields remains close to the current level until the middle of this century. This corresponds to a global decadal mean temperature increase of up to +2°C relative to preindustrial levels. Under a high emission scenario, with approximately +5°C warming by the end of this century, the irrigation effect is projected to decrease to approximately 64% of the current level. Absolute crop production is projected to decrease by approximately 19%, while irrigation-induced production gains decline to approximately 53% of the current levels under the present distribution of irrigated cropland. These results suggest that the effectiveness of irrigation as a buffer against crop water stress diminishes with warming. This highlights the importance of understanding how climate-driven changes in crop water demand and supply constrain irrigation effectiveness.
